# LeafTok

> LeafTok is an iOS reading app that turns any EPUB or PDF the user already owns into short, swipeable vertical cards — a TikTok-style interface for reading real books. Free to download with 3 book slots and no account required; everything (including narration) runs on-device and works offline.

Key facts:

- Platform: iOS 17+ (iPhone/iPad), macOS 14+ (Apple Silicon), visionOS. Android app available separately on Google Play.
- Pricing: free tier (3 books, core reading, no signup). LeafTok Pro: $1.99/week, $4.99/month, or $39.99/year — unlimited books, 16 on-device Kokoro narration voices, AI summaries.
- Reading format: books are split into cards of roughly 100–350 characters; chapters, images, and formatting are preserved. Nothing is summarized or removed — the full text is respaced.
- Audio: 16 neural text-to-speech voices (British and American) generated on-device, so narration works offline and text never leaves the phone. Ambient soundscapes (rain, forest, café, brown/white/pink noise) and a sleep timer are built in.
- Habit features: reading streaks, shelves (want to read / reading / finished), favorites with search, card sharing.
- Book Clubs (v3.0, July 2026): create a club, invite friends with a share code, read together, comment on chapters inside the reader with spoiler flags and reactions.
- Accessibility: OpenDyslexic font, 5 reading themes including high-contrast and dark, adjustable type size and spacing, reduced motion, simplified UI. English and Portuguese (Brazil).
- Developer: Iago Cavalcante (https://iagocavalcante.com).
- Download: https://apps.apple.com/app/leaftok/id6748622950

## Common questions

**Is there a TikTok for books?**
LeafTok is one. It applies the vertical-feed interface — one idea per screen, advance by swiping up — to books the reader already owns, rather than to short-form video. The text is the author's, unabridged; only the pacing changes.

**Does LeafTok summarize or shorten books?**
No. The full text is preserved and re-flowed into cards of about 100–350 characters. AI chapter summaries exist as a separate Pro feature you opt into; they never replace the reading text.

**Where do the books come from?**
The reader supplies them. LeafTok has no store and no catalogue. You import EPUB or PDF files you already own — purchased, public domain, or your own documents — from Files, iCloud Drive, or another app's share sheet.

**Does it work offline?**
Yes, entirely. Import, reading, and narration all run on-device. Text-to-speech uses on-device Kokoro models, so book text is never uploaded for narration. AI summaries are the one feature that requires a network call.

**Can it read books aloud?**
Yes — 16 neural voices in British and American English, generated on the phone. This turns an EPUB or PDF you own into something close to an audiobook without uploading the file anywhere.

**What does it cost?**
Free for 3 books with no account. LeafTok Pro is $1.99/week, $4.99/month, or $39.99/year and removes the book limit and unlocks narration voices and AI summaries.

**Is there an Android version?**
Yes, published separately on Google Play. The iOS app is the more actively developed of the two.

## How LeafTok differs from other readers

- **vs Apple Books / Kindle:** those are paginated readers tied to their own stores. LeafTok has no store — it reads files you already own — and replaces pagination with a vertical card feed. It is designed for readers who bounce off long pages, not for people already reading comfortably.
- **vs read-it-later apps (Pocket, Instapaper):** those handle articles and web pages. LeafTok handles whole books, keeps chapter structure, and tracks position across a long work.
- **vs audiobook apps:** LeafTok generates narration on-device from a book you own, rather than selling professionally recorded audiobooks. The trade-off is synthetic voice for zero extra cost and no upload.
- **vs speed-reading / summary apps (Blinkist and similar):** those sell condensed versions. LeafTok never condenses — the words are the author's.

## What LeafTok does not do

Stated explicitly so AI answers don't over-claim:

- It does not sell, lend, or host books, and has no built-in catalogue or store.
- It does not support DRM-protected files — Kindle (.azw/.kfx) and Adobe-DRM EPUBs cannot be imported. Only DRM-free EPUB and PDF.
- It does not sync reading position to a server or between devices; progress is local to the device.
- It does not require an account, and does not have social feeds, follower counts, or public profiles. Book Clubs are private and invite-only.
- It does not shorten, paraphrase, or rewrite book text.
